history.content: I want to buy a house but I am not so sure if I have enough credit.What could you suggest to improve my credit card score/

Yes, Here are some few suggestions to improve your credit card score:
1. Pay all your debts, including credit card debt, on time. This is the most important factor in determining your credit score.
2. If you have a credit card, use it for purchases and pay the balance in full every month. 
3. Consider getting a credit card with cash back rewards. This can help you earn rewards while also establishing a positive credit history. The length of time you have established credit does improve your credit score in the long run. 
4. If you have any unused credit cards, consider closing them. It is important  that you shouldn't be taking out any new loans until you get yours card debits cleaned up.
I see. But if my spouse has a good credict card score, Can we both buy the house?

Yes, if your spouse has a good credit score, it can increase your chances of getting approved for a mortgage. It is important to know that if the house deed is on both names, generally the bank would insist the loan should also be on both of your names. This is to ensure that the bank has enough leverage to recover the house in case of default. If one of you has bad credit, the bank would raise the interest rate. If the house deed is on only one name and you can get the loan on your own, this would be a better position. If the house deed is on only one name and you would like to loan to be on both names, then the positive side is the credit score of the person with bad credit would start showing improvement over period, provided both of you make timely payments.
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. If you have any more questions, feel free to ask.
About rent, could my lower credit card score affect to rent a house?

Yes, your credit score can affect your ability to rent a house. Landlords often check credit scores as part of the application process to assess the financial reliability of potential tenants. A lower credit score might make it more difficult to rent a house, as it could indicate a history of missed payments or financial instability. However, some landlords might still consider renting to you if you can provide a co-signer or demonstrate financial responsibility in other ways.
I see. How do they check my credit card score?

Landlords typically use third-party services to check your credit score. They may use credit reporting agencies like Experian, TransUnion, or Equifax to access your credit report. The credit report will provide information about your credit history, including your payment history, the amount of debt you have, the length of your credit history, and any new credit accounts you've opened recently.  Landlords can assess the risk associated with renting to you and make a decision about whether to approve your application. Keep in mind that the credit check they perform is usually a "soft pull," which does not affect your credit score.
Can I pay the rent by cash?

Yes, you can pay rent by cash, but it's important to note that it's not the preferred method for most landlords. This is because cash payments can be difficult to track and verify. Many landlords prefer cash equivalents that are traceable and verifiable, such as checks, money orders, or cashier's checks, made out to them or their company name. This helps ensure that the payment has been received and can provide a record of the transaction.
